title: Fpqc coverings detect openness of subsets
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I any index type, and g_i : T_i → S an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let V be a subset of the underlying topological space of S. If g_i^{-1}(V) is open in T_i for every i, then V is open in S.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, affine reduction and openness argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03N0

proof.text: Reduce to the affine open cover of S using isOpenCover_opensRange.isOpen_iff_inter. Package the given family as a Scheme.Cover fpqcPrecoverage and pull it back along each affine-cover map. The pullback equation and continuity show that all inverse images of the restricted subset are open. Fpqc base-change stability supplies the pulled-back covering hypothesis.

For S = Spec R, the qc component of the covering gives QuasiCompactCover of its underlying flat cover, via presieve₀_mem_qcPrecoverage_iff. Apply Mathlib QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom (Cover/QuasiCompact.lean) to obtain a finite affine flat cover F and a morphism e : F.cover → E.forgetQc. This realizes the finite affine refinement required by Definition 022B, without passing to coordinate-ring products.

Form p = Sigma.desc F.cover.f. Finite index types are small in the scheme universe (Countable.toSmall), so the coproduct exists even when the original index universe is larger. Flatness follows componentwise, and F.cover.iUnion_range gives Surjective.sigmaDesc_of_union_range_eq_univ. The source is a finite coproduct of affine schemes, hence affine, and the target is affine, so p is quasi-compact. On each summand, e.w₀ identifies the structure map with e.h₀ j followed by the original g (e.s₀ j); continuity and hV give open preimages there. The open cover sigmaOpenCover then gives IsOpen (p ⁻¹' V).

Apply Flat.isQuotientMap_of_surjective p and its isOpen_preimage equivalence to deduce openness on Spec R. The first local reduction yields openness on S. All finite-coproduct and cover arguments allow an empty family, so the empty-base case is included.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03N0 openness argument, using the finite affine refinement of Topologies Tag 022B and the coproduct quotient-map argument of Morphisms Tag 02JY; implemented directly with Mathlib by U1 on 2026-10-12.

mathlib_searches.query: An fpqc family detects whether a subset of the base scheme is open
mathlib_searches.results: Zariski topology, QuasiCompactCover.of_isOpenMap, reduce_to_affine_global; no fpqc family openness criterion.
Scheme.GlueData.isOpen_iff and quasi-compact/open-immersion results; no fpqc family openness criterion.

Flat.isQuotientMap_of_surjective for a single quasi-compact flat surjection, and the existing StandardFpqcQuotientTopology theorem for finite affine families; neither states the general-family criterion. Project-wide source search found no existing general fpqc openness detection theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem isOpen_of_fpqc_preimages
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} {T : I → Scheme.{u}}
    (g : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S)
    (hg : Presieve.ofArrows T g ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (V : Set S) (hV : ∀ i, IsOpen (g i ⁻¹' V)) : IsOpen V
